showcase_workers_description: Browser thread offload and a claim-based queue worker — the two things the word actually means.
showcase_workers_meanings_intro: "Worker" names three unrelated things. They share a word and nothing else, so it is worth separating them before anything else.
showcase_workers_meaning_thread_desc: A second JavaScript thread in the browser. Runs computation so the UI keeps responding.
showcase_workers_meaning_queue_desc: A consumer that pulls units of work off a queue. Lives on the server.
showcase_workers_meaning_service_desc: A network proxy for a PWA. Unrelated to both of the above —
showcase_workers_meanings_tell: The tell: ask what it consumes. A queue worker consumes from a queue, a Web Worker consumes messages you send it, a service worker consumes fetch events. A job consumes nothing — it wakes on a timer and runs.
showcase_workers_thread_intro: Both buttons below run the exact same function — decode the image, downscale it, then walk every pixel to build a colour histogram. The only variable is which thread it runs on. Watch the dial, not the palette.
showcase_workers_thread_transfer_note: The worker path transfers the ArrayBuffer rather than copying it: postMessage(data, [buffer]) moves ownership and neuters the sender's copy. On a large photo that is the difference between a copy and a pointer hand-off — and it is the most-missed part of the API.
showcase_workers_thread_unsupported: This browser lacks OffscreenCanvas or createImageBitmap, so the demo cannot run here.
showcase_workers_thread_error_type: That file is not an image.
showcase_workers_thread_drop: Drop an image here or click to browse
showcase_workers_thread_drop_hint: Nothing is uploaded — the whole analysis happens in your browser
showcase_workers_thread_probe: Animation probe — driven by requestAnimationFrame, so it stops whenever the main thread is blocked
showcase_workers_thread_verdict: Longest blocked frame: {main} ms on the main thread versus {worker} ms in the worker. The work took roughly as long either way — what changed is whether the page could draw while it ran.
showcase_workers_queue_running_note: This deployment is persistent ({platform}), so the worker is resident: it claims a batch every {seconds} seconds.
showcase_workers_queue_dormant_note: This deployment is serverless ({platform}), so no process survives the response and the worker cannot be resident. A daily cron drains the queue instead. The dormancy is the lesson, not a defect — it is why the whole job system is push-triggered.
showcase_workers_queue_intro: The notification outbox is a real queue table, and this is its consumer. Work is taken with one atomic statement: rows are locked, marked, and returned together, so two workers can never take the same row.
showcase_workers_queue_fence_note: The attempt counter doubles as a fence token. If a worker dies mid-send, the reaper requeues its row after the lease expires — and because a re-claim bumps the counter, the dead worker's late write no longer matches and is discarded instead of corrupting the row.
showcase_workers_not_jobs_intro: This project's background work is made of jobs, not workers. The distinction is not pedantry — it decides whether you need a queue at all.
showcase_workers_not_jobs_job_desc: A unit of work. Something wakes it and tells it what to run. Costs nothing when idle because it does not exist when idle.
showcase_workers_not_jobs_worker_desc: A process that is already running and asks the queue what is due. Costs money while idle, and gives you retries and fast pickup in exchange.
showcase_workers_not_jobs_outro: Everything scheduled here is pushed rather than pulled: a cron, an interval, or an admin click names the work directly.
showcase_wasm_description: Rust compiled to WebAssembly, raced against plain JavaScript on identical work — boundary costs on display instead of hidden.
showcase_wasm_pattern_intro: A Rust crate compiled to a 20 KB wasm module, vendored into the repo and loaded with zero Vite plugins. The dev container never needs a Rust toolchain: a throwaway builder container compiles the crate, and the generated glue and binary are committed like any other source.
showcase_wasm_pattern_kernel_body: Pixels live in wasm linear memory. JS writes them through a view once, filter calls cross the boundary with two scalars, and a vitest parity gate keeps the Rust and JS implementations byte-identical.
showcase_wasm_pattern_build_body: One host-side script, one ephemeral Rust container, artifacts committed. Reproducibility is pinned by a digest-pinned builder image, rust-toolchain.toml and Cargo.lock — and a committed build manifest turns the gate red if sources and artifacts drift apart.
showcase_wasm_pattern_loader_body: ?url plus an explicit init call sidesteps every known dev-vs-build wasm divergence in Vite and SvelteKit — no wasm plugin, no top-level await, nothing executed during SSR.
showcase_wasm_lab_intro: The same filter, implemented line-for-line in Rust and JavaScript, over the same synthetic frame. Both engines run in the same worker, the lane order alternates every round, and checksums prove the outputs are identical — algorithm, input, worker and output are controlled; what remains is the language and its runtime.
showcase_wasm_lab_unsupported: This browser does not support WebAssembly, which this demo needs.
showcase_wasm_lab_loading: Waking up the lab — this demo runs entirely in your browser.
showcase_wasm_lab_no_copy: No boundary stages — the data already lives in JS memory, which is exactly the asymmetry the wasm lane has to beat.
showcase_wasm_lab_verdict: Compute: wasm ran {compute}× the speed of JS. End-to-end with boundary copies: {total}×.
showcase_wasm_lab_protocol: {warmup} warm-up rounds discarded, {rounds} timed rounds with the engine order alternating each round, medians reported. End-to-end means JS-owned input to JS-owned output; harness resets stay untimed.
showcase_wasm_lab_init: The first run paid {ms} ms once for fetch + compile + instantiate.
showcase_wasm_boundary_intro: One multiply per element over a million floats — almost no compute per byte moved. Three lanes: plain JS, wasm that copies the array across the boundary on every call, and wasm with the data resident in linear memory. Marshalling losing to plain JS is the point.
showcase_wasm_boundary_checksums: All three lanes produced bit-identical results.
showcase_wasm_boundary_verdict: Same multiply, three costs: JS {js} ms, copied wasm {copied} ms, resident wasm {resident} ms per round. The gap is boundary marshalling and allocation — glue, a fresh buffer and two copies on every call.
showcase_wasm_honesty_intro: A benchmark that flatters wasm is easy: time cold JS against warm wasm, hide the copies, report the best run. Every number on this page follows five rules instead:
showcase_wasm_honesty_warmup: Warm-up rounds run both engines untimed first — un-warmed JS executes in the interpreter rather than the JIT and loses by default.
showcase_wasm_honesty_interleave: Timed rounds are counterbalanced — which engine goes first alternates every round; a fixed order keeps position bias even in dedicated benchmark libraries.
showcase_wasm_honesty_median: Medians with min–max spread, never means — one GC pause must not move the headline number.
showcase_wasm_honesty_first_run: The one-time fetch + compile + instantiate cost is shown, not hidden — it is the real price of adopting wasm.
showcase_wasm_honesty_breakdown: Boundary copies are timed as their own stages — end-to-end wins are the only wins that count.
showcase_wasm_honesty_engine_note: Results are engine-dependent: the same workload can differ by nearly an order of magnitude between browsers. This page reports your engine's numbers, not a universal truth.
showcase_wasm_when_intro: Wasm is not performance pixie dust — JavaScript JITs to machine code too, and a warmed JIT can approach or beat wasm on numeric loops. Wasm earns its place when the work is compute-dense and the data crosses the boundary rarely.
showcase_wasm_when_wins_1: Dense numeric kernels over typed arrays — convolution, physics, signal processing — with the data resident in linear memory.
showcase_wasm_when_wins_2: Predictability: wasm's run-to-run spread is typically tighter — ahead-of-time compilation, no JIT tiers or deopts to fall out of.
showcase_wasm_when_wins_3: Reusing an existing Rust or C++ implementation instead of porting it by hand.
showcase_wasm_when_loses_1: String-heavy work — every string crosses the boundary as a UTF-16 → UTF-8 transcode plus a copy.
showcase_wasm_when_loses_2: Chatty APIs that copy buffers per call — the marshalling lane above pays for the same lesson.
showcase_wasm_when_loses_3: Allocation-heavy object graphs — engine GCs are deeply optimized for them, while a wasm module ships and warms its own allocator.
showcase_wasm_when_note: This repo already runs wasm in production — server-side: shiki's Oniguruma engine highlighted every code block on this page roughly five times faster than its pure-JS fallback.

showcase_analytics_journeys_desc_transit: Which page follows which, ranked by how often the move happens
showcase_analytics_journeys_empty_transi: A transition needs two pageviews in one session. Browse a few pages and they will appear here.
showcase_analytics_journeys_desc_session: Last 20 visitor sessions with page counts and duration
showcase_analytics_journeys_method_note: Counted with a window function over consecutive pageviews in the same session. Reloads are excluded — they are not navigations. Aggregate paths merge visitors with very different intentions, so read this as “what moves are common”, not “why people move”.
showcase_analytics_mydata_reveal_intro: See exactly what the analytics system can detect about your current visit — grouped by consent tier.
showcase_analytics_mydata_note_country: Resolved from your connection at the edge, not read from your device — which is why it needs no consent.
showcase_analytics_mydata_note_confirm: One consent-free ping proves your browser ran JavaScript (separating you from crawlers), and your connection is classed once against published datacenter/relay ranges — the class is stored, your address never.
showcase_analytics_mydata_note_device_br: Derived from the User-Agent below — kept deliberately coarse, never a version number.
showcase_analytics_mydata_note_navigatio: Which page follows which, within one session.
showcase_analytics_mydata_never_title: What is never collected, at any tier
showcase_analytics_mydata_never_item_rec: Session recordings or replays of your screen
showcase_analytics_mydata_never_item_for: Anything you type into a form
showcase_analytics_mydata_never_item_ip: Your raw IP address, in any table
showcase_analytics_mydata_never_item_fin: Fingerprinting signals — screen size, timezone, canvas, installed fonts
showcase_analytics_mydata_never_item_sha: Any identifier shared with another site, or with a third party
showcase_analytics_mydata_never_note: The visitor hash is built from your IP and User-Agent alone. Adding any further signal would make it a fingerprint, so nothing further is added — that is a design constraint, not a current setting.
showcase_analytics_mydata_hash_desc: Your IP and User-Agent are hashed into an irreversible visitor ID — the raw values are never stored.
showcase_analytics_mydata_toast_export: In production, this would export all data associated with your visitor ID as a JSON download (GDPR Art 20).
showcase_analytics_mydata_toast_delete: In production, this would delete all events and sessions linked to your visitor ID (GDPR Art 17).
showcase_analytics_privacy_desc_consent: How visitors have configured their consent preferences
showcase_analytics_privacy_desc_retentio: How long analytics data is stored before automatic deletion
showcase_analytics_privacy_desc_verifica: Live proof that privacy measures are active
showcase_analytics_privacy_retention_not: Individual pageviews, actions, and timing events
Daily rollups — no individual visitor data
IP addresses are never stored in raw form
showcase_analytics_privacy_verify_hashin: All visitor IDs are SHA-256 hashed before storage. Format:
showcase_analytics_privacy_verify_consen: Device and browser fields are NULL for 'necessary' consent tier visitors; country is connection-derived and present at every tier
showcase_analytics_privacy_verify_noip_d: No column in the schema stores raw IP addresses
showcase_analytics_privacy_verify_server: Server-side pageview log plus consent-gated first-party beacons; one consent-free confirmation ping reads nothing from your device. Vercel Web Analytics loads only after consent.
showcase_analytics_privacy_verify_seed_d: Demo uses deterministic faker seed (42) — zero real user data
showcase_analytics_live_desc_feed: Real-time analytics events as they occur (simulated for demo)
showcase_analytics_live_empty_desc: Simulated events will appear here shortly.
showcase_analytics_funnels_desc_funnel: Tracks visitors from landing page through docs and pricing to signup
showcase_analytics_funnels_desc_breakdow: Detailed metrics for each funnel step
showcase_analytics_funnels_alert_desc: No funnel data found for the selected range. Try reseeding the analytics data from the Overview page.

showcase_3d_static_description: GLTF model with orbit controls and directional lighting.
showcase_viz_charts_description: Bar, line, area, pie, radar, bubble, sparkline, gauge, and treemap charts. SimpleChart and Sparkline/Gauge are zero-dependency SVG. The rest use Chart.js or d3-hierarchy.

app_notifications_push_unsupported: This browser doesn't support push notifications.

showcase_pwa_description: Installable app shell with an honest offline story — manifest, service worker, caching contract, update flow.
pwa_manifest_description: Full-stack reference and test sandbox — proven patterns for SvelteKit, AI, and data.
showcase_ui_description: Complete UI component library and design tokens
showcase_db_description: PostgreSQL, Neo4j, R2, Redis — connections, types, queries, and storage
showcase_ai_description: The two AI surfaces, X-rayed: chatbot and deskbot layer by layer — guard, prompt, retrieval, tools, gates.
showcase_toolkits_description: Bundled, multi-step tools — upload once, run an AI pipeline, adjust the results, then approve. Nothing is saved.
showcase_observability_description: Honest performance measurement: separating real telemetry from your own dev traffic, and turning budgets into tests.
showcase_obs_overview_lead: A performance dashboard is only as good as the data behind it. This one measures two different things and refuses to mix them: field telemetry from real visitors, and lab measurements taken from a production build.
showcase_obs_overview_field_desc: Core Web Vitals at the 75th percentile, from visitors at the analytics consent tier. Scored against Google's published bands, so the verdict matches what Search Console reports.
showcase_obs_overview_lane_title: …and how much of it is real
showcase_obs_overview_lane_desc: Every number above reads the production lane only. This is the split it was filtered from — shown rather than hidden, because an aggregate that quietly drops rows looks identical to one with nothing to drop.
showcase_obs_overview_lane_note: Production traffic is {pct}% of collected samples. If that share moves sharply, the filter is the first thing to check — not the site.
showcase_obs_overview_lab_title: Lab: what the last build weighs
showcase_obs_overview_lab_desc: Bundle size never shows up in real-user data until it has already shipped. These come from a production build, committed to the repository so growth is visible in review.
showcase_obs_honesty_lead: The dev server was writing telemetry into the production analytics database. That is a common mistake and an unusually nasty one, because of which direction it skews the numbers.
showcase_obs_honesty_problem_body: Dev samples come from localhost: no network, no TLS, no cold start. They do not add symmetric noise around the truth — they drag every latency percentile downward. Over one 30-day window, 72% of collected samples were dev rows, and first-byte latency read far better than reality.
showcase_obs_honesty_direction: The contaminated figure was {pct}% better than the truth. Noise you can spot; flattery you cannot — nothing about the number invites suspicion.
showcase_obs_honesty_fingerprint_body: No extra column and no backfill were needed. The attribution build records the CSS selector of the element it blamed, and Svelte's scope-class format differs between builds — so every sample already carries a fingerprint of the build that produced it.
showcase_obs_honesty_fingerprint_note: The dev pattern is anchored so it cannot match the production prefix: it requires a hyphen immediately after the s, and svelte- has a v there. A discriminator that matched both would filter out every real sample and show an empty production lane on a perfectly healthy deployment.
showcase_obs_honesty_live_desc: Classified across the last 30 days of this site's own telemetry. A session showing any dev marker is treated as dev — losing a real session costs one sample, keeping a dev one costs the accuracy of every percentile it lands in.
showcase_obs_honesty_rule_body: Fixing the source is necessary but not sufficient. The read-side filter is what makes the fix durable:
showcase_obs_honesty_rule_1: Fix the source — gate telemetry on a production check, so no new bad rows are written.
showcase_obs_honesty_rule_2: Filter on read anyway — rows already written stay inside the retention window and keep skewing every aggregate over them.
showcase_obs_honesty_rule_3: Report what you excluded — a count that can rise is the only thing that notices if the source-side gate ever regresses.
showcase_obs_budgets_lead: Budgets are worth little if nothing enforces them, and unenforceable if they fail on the day they land. This separates the two jobs: targets say where we want to be, ratchets stop today's number becoming tomorrow's floor.
showcase_obs_budgets_target_desc: Where the build should get to. Scored and displayed, never build-failing.
showcase_obs_budgets_target_note: The heaviest route is well over its target, and saying so plainly is the point. A dashboard that only shows green has stopped being a measurement.
showcase_obs_budgets_ratchet_desc: The measured value at the moment it was accepted. These fail the build when exceeded, and only ever move down — lowering one is how an improvement gets banked.
showcase_obs_budgets_gate_body: Not everything belongs in a gate. Bundle weight is unusually well suited to one:
showcase_obs_budgets_gate_1: It is invisible in review — a one-line import can add a hundred kilobytes with nothing in the diff to show it.
showcase_obs_budgets_gate_2: It is deterministic — the same source produces the same number, so the check does not flake.
showcase_obs_budgets_gate_3: It is only catchable before shipping — by the time real-user data reflects it, users have already downloaded it.
consent_banner_blurb: Some help us understand how the site is used. You choose which ones we set.
consent_tier_necessary_desc: Required for the site to work. Cannot be turned off.
consent_tier_analytics_desc: Page views, device type, and how you move between pages.
admin_perf_subtitle: Field telemetry and build measurements, read with the dev lane filtered out.
admin_perf_panel_lanes_desc: Which build produced each sample. Every panel below reads the production lane only — this is what that leaves out.
admin_perf_lane_dev_present: {count} samples came from a dev server and are excluded. Historic rows inside the retention window are expected; a rising count means the dev-side gate regressed.
admin_perf_panel_field_desc: Real-user Core Web Vitals from visitors at the analytics consent tier, scored against Google's bands.
admin_perf_panel_idlegap_desc: First-byte latency grouped by how long the platform sat idle before the visit, counting crawler traffic. Read it as a shape, not as a cause.
admin_perf_gap_insufficient: Too few samples to read as a trend. Shown for completeness — do not draw a conclusion from it.
admin_perf_panel_lab_desc: Measured from a production build and committed to the repo, so bundle growth shows up in review instead of in production.
admin_perf_lab_devmode: This snapshot was taken with NODE_ENV={env}. A dev-mode build inflates client JS by roughly 9%, so these numbers cannot be compared against the ceilings. Regenerate it from a production build.
admin_perf_lab_stale: Snapshot is {days} days old. Regenerate it after a production build to see current numbers.
admin_perf_ratchet_desc: What the build may not exceed. This is the half that fails CI; the targets above are where we want to end up.
admin_perf_panel_hotpaths_desc: Server-rendered pageviews per route, beside crawler hits on the same route. Client-side navigations never reach the origin and are excluded.
admin_analytics_friction_description: Rage and dead clicks — where visitors get stuck.
admin_analytics_friction_empty: No friction detected in this period.
admin_analytics_userlane_description: Signed-in usage. Separate lane, separate legal basis — not governed by the consent banner.
admin_analytics_userlane_empty: No account activity in this period.
admin_analytics_audience_description: Unique visitors by origin and client. Counted per person, not per session.
admin_analytics_audience_coverage_geo: Country resolved for {known} of {total} visitors — read at the edge from the connection, so it is available at every consent tier.
admin_analytics_audience_coverage_client: Device and browser known for {known} of {total} visitors. These come from the User-Agent, which is only read at the analytics consent tier — so this is a breakdown of consenting visitors, not of everyone.
credits_meta_description: The open-source projects and hosted services v10r runs on, with links to their docs and the showcase that proves each integration.
credits_lede: v10r is built on the open-source projects and hosted services below. Every entry links to its official site, the in-app docs, and the showcase that proves the integration works.
credits_outro_source: This page covers the headline stack. For the complete inventory — every dependency, its version, and its license — see package.json in the public repository.
credits_outro_license: Velociraptor itself is released under the MIT license.

credits_role_paraglide: compiled, tree-shakeable i18n messages for en, de, and ru

credits_role_vitest: the test runner behind the validation gate
showcase_ai_claim_chatbot: The v10r expert: read-only, grounded, citation-faithful. One orchestrator, one guard, five retrieval tools — and not a single way to mutate anything.
showcase_ai_claim_deskbot: The in-desk operator: agentic and mutating — but a write can only run once, and only after a human said yes.
showcase_ai_claim_guard: Four gates reject before a single token is spent — identical on both surfaces, deliberately.
showcase_ai_claim_prompt_chatbot: The prompt is assembled cache-stable-first; the chatbot skips every desk block.
showcase_ai_claim_prompt_deskbot: The prompt’s variable tail is your live desk — and it is escaped for a reason.
showcase_ai_claim_nrag_chatbot: One retrieval kernel, system-owned corpus — and exactly one tier actually live.
showcase_ai_claim_nrag_deskbot: Same kernel, your files, no graph tier — refreshed off the hot path.
showcase_ai_claim_tools_chatbot: Five read-only tools, no scope field, zero overlap with the desk set.
showcase_ai_claim_tools_deskbot: Thirteen scoped tools, zero overlap with retrieval — and the mutating ones cannot run in-loop.
showcase_ai_claim_verify: After the stream closes, every citation is checked against the sources the model actually saw.
showcase_ai_claim_approval: A write can only run once, and only after a human said yes — approval binds execution.
showcase_ai_claim_stream: A turn is a chain of attempts, not one call: providers rotate on 429 with a cooldown.
showcase_ai_claim_awareness_chatbot: Site-awareness is one route label — deliberately thin.
showcase_ai_claim_awareness_deskbot: Desk-awareness is your open panels — deliberately deep. The asymmetry is the design.
showcase_ai_role_client_chatbot: Vely — the persistent, minimizable panel; one singleton thread survives navigation.
showcase_ai_role_client_deskbot: The desk chat panel — scopes are consent switches the user flips per turn.
showcase_ai_role_route: Thin adapter: bounded JSON read, Valibot parse, explicit surface — no logic lives here.
showcase_ai_role_guard: auth → configured → rate-limit → daily budget; one shared function, so the limit key cannot drift.
showcase_ai_role_orchestrator: One function serves both surfaces; they diverge at exactly one discriminant.
showcase_ai_role_compaction: Oversized tool results become refs the model can pull back — the context window is a budget.
showcase_ai_role_prompt: Cache-stable prefix first, volatile tail last; conditional blocks vanish with their predicate.
showcase_ai_role_retrieval_chatbot: System docs + catalog corpus behind one tenancy filter; llmwiki pointers first, drill on demand.
showcase_ai_role_retrieval_deskbot: Your own desk files through the same kernel — synced off the hot path by a polling job.
showcase_ai_role_harness_chatbot: Five read-only retrieval tools; the loop is capped at 3 steps.
showcase_ai_role_harness_deskbot: Scope-gated desk tools; 3 steps read-only, 5 when a mutating scope is granted.
showcase_ai_role_gate_chatbot: Post-stream: every citation is verified against the chunks the model actually drilled.
showcase_ai_role_gate_deskbot: Write/destructive tools return a sentinel; the mutation runs only via the human-approved replay.
showcase_ai_role_stream: streamText attempts rotate providers on 429 (60s cooldown); a leak guard gags tool-call markup typed as text.
showcase_ai_role_persist: onFinish: messages, steps and tool calls are saved; tokens are charged against the daily budget.
showcase_ai_guard_auth_gloss: No session — nothing else even runs.
showcase_ai_guard_configured_gloss: No provider key in the environment — honest 503, not a broken chat.
showcase_ai_guard_ratelimit_gloss: Per-user sliding window; the 429 carries Retry-After.
showcase_ai_guard_budget_gloss: A daily per-user token cap — spend is charged after each turn.
showcase_ai_flow_aria: Request flow through the functional layers
showcase_ai_prov_recorded: Recorded turn · demo workspace · {date} · nothing was mutated
showcase_ai_prov_live: Live turn · your account · real tokens are spent
showcase_ai_halt_hint: Playback stopped — the agent proposed a plan. The next frame is your decision.
showcase_ai_tools_shared_line: {own} tools on this surface · {other} on the sibling · 0 shared
showcase_ai_tools_scope_footnote: Mounting is scope-dependent per turn: desk_propose_plan mounts only when a mutating scope is granted, and with no scopes the desk harness mounts zero tools.
showcase_ai_nrag_tenancy: One tenancy filter is the whole corpus boundary: document.userId — the kernel is never forked.
showcase_ai_nrag_sync: Freshness is reconciled off the hot path: a job polls desk.file.updatedAt — saves never block on embedding.
showcase_ai_prompt_cache_boundary: cache boundary — everything above is byte-stable across turns
showcase_ai_prompt_est_badge: chars/4 estimate, not a provider count
showcase_ai_prompt_escape_note: Unescaped panel content containing </panel></desk-context> would close the block early and the rest would read as prompt — escapeXmlText is load-bearing.
showcase_ai_aware_site: A single server-resolved route label, public-catalog routes only — never the raw path, never the DOM.
showcase_ai_aware_desk: Which panels and files are open, with content (≤8000 chars each) — secrets scrubbed, XML escaped.
showcase_ai_aware_redacted: Secret-shaped strings are scrubbed before the model sees the panel.
showcase_ai_stream_leakguard: Some models type their tool call as text instead of calling it. A transform sniffs text deltas and gags the leak for the rest of the step — the turn degrades to empty instead of leaking markup.
showcase_ai_door_note_quota: A live turn spends your daily AI budget. The recorded trace on this page costs nothing.
showcase_ai_door_note_unconfigured: No AI provider is configured in this environment — the recorded trace above is fully functional regardless.
showcase_ai_sibling_chatbot: The sibling surface: read-only, grounded, citation-faithful.
showcase_ai_sibling_deskbot: The sibling surface: agentic, mutating, approval-gated.
showcase_ai_replay_second_stack: The approval replay is a separate HTTP request — possibly minutes later. It gets its own stack; the shared proposal id is the only link.
showcase_ai_approval_ttl: The 15-minute consent window lives in the SQL predicate, not in JS — no time-of-check gap.
showcase_ai_approval_norollback: First failing step short-circuits and keeps partial results — there is no rollback; recovery is the pre-image file revision.
showcase_ai_approval_frozen: The replay runs under grantedScopes frozen at proposal time — approval cannot widen the grant that was reviewed.
showcase_ai_verify_chips: Verdicts become the citation chips on the answer: quote, paraphrase, drifted, uncited.
showcase_ai_claim_probe_chatbot: Type any question and watch the grounding decision happen: what each corpus had available, what the ranker chose, and which prompt blocks are fixed context versus ingested for this exact query. The probe runs the SAME assembly code as a real turn — it just never calls the model.
showcase_ai_claim_probe_deskbot: The deskbot's per-query dynamics are different: retrieval runs over YOUR desk files, and the plan governor decides from the phrasing whether the planning block is injected. Try a destructive wording and watch it flip.
showcase_ai_probe_input_label: Ask anything — see what would ground the answer
showcase_ai_probe_note: Retrieval-only: the probe runs the same gates, retrieval, and prompt assembly as a real turn but never calls the model — worst case one embedding.
showcase_ai_probe_signin: Sign in to probe with your own questions — the recorded examples work without an account.
showcase_ai_probe_gate_ground_gloss: Trivial turns (greetings, acks, very short messages) skip the embedding and ALL retrieval — nothing is spent on chit-chat.
showcase_ai_probe_gate_deixis_gloss: When the question points at the current page (“how does this work?”), the embed query is seeded with the resolved page title and breadcrumb.
showcase_ai_probe_gate_plan_gloss: A granted mutating scope PLUS destructive phrasing injects the planning block — the model must propose a plan before touching anything.
showcase_ai_probe_skip_gated: Skipped — the relevance gate closed; no embedding was spent.
showcase_ai_probe_skip_scope: Not mounted — the desk:ask scope is not granted this turn.
showcase_ai_probe_skip_empty: Skipped — nothing is ingested on this lane yet.
showcase_ai_probe_tools_line: {n} tools mounted — mounting is per surface and scope, never per query; which tool actually fires is the model's call at generation time.
showcase_ai_probe_cutoff: production cutoff: top {n} enter the prompt
showcase_ai_probe_err_auth: Sign in to run a live probe.
showcase_ai_probe_err_rate: Rate limit reached — try again in a moment.
showcase_ai_probe_err_unavailable: No AI provider is configured right now.
showcase_ai_probe_lane_error: Retrieval failed on this lane — a real turn would proceed without it.
showcase_ai_probe_galaxy_caveat: Star positions and background dust are illustrative — the ranked list below is the factual record.
